title: Qatayef with Cheese: Fried Pancake Half-Moons with Melting Cheese and Syrup
changes_from_base: a thinner yeasted batter, closed half-moons filled with melting white cheese, deep-fried at 175 °C and dipped in warm syrup instead of left half-open with cream
summary: Yeasted pancakes folded around mild white cheese, crimped into half-moons, fried crisp and dipped in warm syrup.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted mozzarella or akkawi, finely chopped
ingredients.note: if using salty akkawi or nabulsi, soak 1.5 h in hot water, changing it once, then squeeze dry

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, salt and warm water until smooth. Cover and leave at room temperature for 1-1.5 h until foamy, with a watery ring around the edge; the yeast gives the pancakes their spongy, holey tops.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Simmer the sugar and 120 ml water for 8 min until it lightly coats a spoon. Add the lemon juice and orange blossom water if using, and keep warm on the lowest heat.

steps.title: Prepare the cheese
steps.text: Pat the chopped cheese dry with kitchen paper. Removing surface moisture stops it steaming inside the pastry and forcing the seams open.

steps.title: Cook the pancakes
steps.text: Whisk the bicarbonate into the batter for a final lift. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat without oil and pour in 2 tbsp portions so each spreads to about 10 cm. Cook on one side only for 1-2 min, until the top is dry and full of holes and the base golden, then keep under a tea towel. You should have 12.

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.text: Spoon about 20 g filling onto the holey side of a pancake and fold it into a half-moon. Pinch the edges firmly together and crimp with a fork. A tight seal stops the filling leaking into the oil.

steps.title: Fry until golden
steps.text: Heat 4 cm of oil to 175 °C and fry 3-4 at a time for about 2 min, turning once, until deep golden and crisp. Frying in small batches keeps the oil hot so they do not turn greasy.

steps.title: Dip in syrup
steps.text: Drain briefly on the rack, then dip each one in the warm syrup for 30 s, turning to coat. Serve warm.

tips: If using akkawi or nabulsi, taste a piece after soaking; it should be mild, not salty.
A common mistake is overfilling, which makes the seams burst. 20 g is plenty.
Eat them warm while the cheese still stretches.
Check the oil between batches and let it return to 175 °C.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten straight after frying. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for 1 day; reheat in a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven for 8-10 min until piping hot.
